title: cross-audit automation run v1
description: The evidence a single generated/existing verification produced, and — critically — how its outcome is CLASSIFIED. `execution_result` separates a genuine product failure from a broken test, a missing environment and an unverified case: PASS | PRODUCT_FAILURE | TEST_INVALID | ENVIRONMENT_FAILURE | NOT_VERIFIED. When `cmd_run` writes this record the classification is DERIVED from structured signals (exit code, positive/negative control, selector resolution) rather than chosen, so a broken selector or an unstartable harness is never scored as a product failure and a green harness that never proved it can fail is never trusted. `adapter_capability_ceiling` is a fixed property of the adapter kind and never above F2: a tool run cannot self-certify an independent oracle. BOUND: the workspace is caller-writable, so a hand-authored record can state any of these fields. Nothing here authenticates that `cmd_run` produced it — that is ADR 0006 attestation, whose promotion gate is closed by decision. The gates downstream check CONSISTENCY (target, plan descriptor, harness bytes, controls), not provenance.

schema_version.description: Exact artifact version. Pinned rather than pattern-matched so a standalone contract check agrees with the runtime gate (crossaudit.common.CURRENT_VERSION): 1.0.0 coverage semantics differ from 1.1.0, so accepting both here would validate artifacts the engine rejects.

run_nonce.description: Per-invocation freshness token. For a report-producing adapter (Playwright/API) the report MUST echo this nonce; a stale/caller-written report that does not carry it cannot yield PASS/PRODUCT_FAILURE.

target_verified.description: Whether the target matched the pinned identity when it was verified, immediately before the disposable execution COPY was materialized. Execution then runs against that copy (cwd/PYTHONPATH), so the original is only read and stays byte-identical; a mismatch (target moved/mutated) fails the run closed before any copy — evidence from a changed target is never fresh.

input_artifacts.description: The baselines/fixtures this run was executed against, with the digest OBSERVED at execution time. Without this the record names which harness the plan declared but not what it compared against, so a later reader cannot tell whether the baseline has since changed.

generated_artifact.description: Provenance of a workspace-authored script that was executed (content-addressed).

exec_snapshot_digest.description: Content digest of the disposable execution COPY the run executed against (the original target is read-only). Bound to the pinned target_digest verified before the copy.

execution_boundary.description: The mechanically-enforced LOCAL write boundary the bound harness ran under (or the record that none was available). Copy isolation alone is NOT a boundary: a harness can compute an absolute path at runtime and write back into the original, which a literal source scan cannot catch. A bound harness may therefore promote PASS/PRODUCT_FAILURE ONLY when `enforced` is true. This is a narrow local-verification boundary — not the ADR 0003 trusted runner and not outward-action attestation; on an unsupported platform it is unenforced and the run stays NOT_VERIFIED.

kind.description: The confinement mechanism. `sandbox-exec` is the macOS system utility driving a generated deny-by-default profile; `none` means no OS-enforced boundary was available.

enforced.description: True only when an OS-level write boundary actually confined the harness. Promotion of PASS/PRODUCT_FAILURE requires this to be true.

write_roots.description: The disposable directories writes were confined to (realpath'd); everything outside is denied.

net_loopback.description: Host-local egress was permitted for this run (run-config granted service/database). The seatbelt loopback rule is all-or-nothing, so true means every host-local address on every port was reachable — a narrower guarantee than the same record with false. Egress off the host stays denied either way.

positive_verified.description: True only when a positive-control mode was actually executed and fresh (echoed the CLI freshness token). A PRODUCT_FAILURE requires harness_bound + positive_verified + positive_control pass.

negative_verified.description: True only when a negative-control/fault-injection mode actually executed and fresh. A material PASS satisfies T2/T3 readiness only when harness_bound + negative_verified + negative_control pass (the oracle demonstrably fails on inverted behavior).

harness_bound.description: True only when the positive/negative controls are the SAME content-addressed harness (`harness.content_hash`) invoked by the CLI in known-good and injected-fault modes with a per-run freshness token. Only harness-bound, fresh controls can promote PASS/PRODUCT_FAILURE; unrelated legacy control commands are recorded but never promote.

assertion.description: Human description of the oracle assertion; the harness's case/fault semantics live in its hashed content and still require reviewer/challenger inspection.

target_contact.description: What of the PINNED TARGET COPY the harness reported touching in its main mode, nonce-bound and read from the harness's own stdout. ABSENT MEANS NOT OBSERVED: a run that never opened the target proved its oracle discriminates, not that the product behaves. Contact is not relevance — a target script that does nothing is still contact — so this never replaces reviewer judgement, it only stops the engine asserting a necessary condition it can see is absent.

selectors.description: Playwright/UI selector provenance: what was targeted, where the selector came from, and whether it resolved. An unresolved selector forces TEST_INVALID, not PRODUCT_FAILURE.

missing.description: true when a referenced artifact was NOT found/readable under the run; the artifact_hash is then a placeholder (sha256 of empty), NOT a content hash of an empty file — a missing artifact is not an empty one.

plan_descriptor_digest.description: Digest of the governing plan item's authored content (every field except provenance) as recorded when this observation was written. Assessment re-derives it from the current plan and refuses the run as backing evidence when it differs, so editing an item in place — new harness, new oracle, new permissions — cannot leave the old run vouching for the new descriptor. BOUND: this detects later EDITS; it does not prove execution history. The value sits in a caller-writable observation, so it binds this record to descriptor content and nothing more. Authenticating that a process actually ran under it is ADR 0006 attestation, whose promotion gate is closed by decision.

control_run.description: A separately EXECUTED control (positive known-good, or negative fault-injection): its own command, exit and stream hashes.
